summary: 资料照片：美籍缅甸裔学者敏辛在尼亚加拉大瀑布留影。(照片摄于2022年4月30日，由敏辛的弟弟Aung Maw Zin提供) 美国多个人权与学术自由组织星期一(11月9日)发出一份联合声明，呼吁美国国会在本届立法会期结束前，通过由两党议员在9月份共同提出的相关决议案，要求中国立即释放美国公民兼学者敏辛(Min Zin)。牵头的弗利基金会(Foley Foundation)告诉美国之音(VOA)，国会两院若能在圣诞节休会前以口头表决方式进行审议，相关决议案有望迅速获得通过。 联
content:
资料照片：美籍缅甸裔学者敏辛在尼亚加拉大瀑布留影。(照片摄于2022年4月30日，由敏辛的弟弟Aung Maw Zin提供)
美国多个人权与学术自由组织星期一(11月9日)发出一份联合声明，呼吁美国国会在本届立法会期结束前，通过由两党议员在9月份共同提出的相关决议案，要求中国立即释放美国公民兼学者敏辛(Min Zin)。牵头的弗利基金会(Foley Foundation)告诉美国之音(VOA)，国会两院若能在圣诞节休会前以口头表决方式进行审议，相关决议案有望迅速获得通过。
联合声明写道，这封致参议院多数党领袖约翰·图恩(John Thune)和众议院议长麦克·约翰逊(Mike Johnson)的信函，已于11月4日送达国会领袖手中。
声明说，该信函敦促参众两院迅速采取行动，通过今年9月由参议员埃德·马基(Ed Markey)、泰德·巴德(Ted Budd)、匡希恒(John Curtis)和亚当·希夫(Adam Schiff)提出的参议院第865号决议案以及由众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)、斯蒂芬·林奇(Stephen Lynch)和金映玉(Young Kim)提出的众议院第1549号决议案。
这些跨党决议案谴责了中共一再任意或非法拘押美国公民的行为模式，敦促美国政府把所有在中国遭非法拘押的美国公民的平安返回当作优先事项，并敦促国务卿使用一切可以使用的工具，督促释放所有被非法或不当关押在中华人民共和国的美国公民。
这些组织在信中写道：“非法拘押无辜的美国公民绝无正当理由，必须予以最强烈的谴责。我们与敏辛先生及其家人站在一起，在他重获自由之前，我们绝不会停止努力。”
美国国务院10月19日更新了对美国公民前往中国的旅行警示，目前虽整体旅行风险仍维持二级，即“提高警觉”(Level 2-Exercise increased caution)，但是在其中加入了“D”标识(代表“非法拘押”风险)。国务院新闻发言人当时告诉美国之音(VOA)，华盛顿认定“美国人在中国面临被非法拘押的严重风险”。
美国国务院也在其官网提醒美国公民进入中国大陆时务必提高警觉，因为“当地法律的执行存在任意性，且可能在缺乏公平、透明法律程序的情况下实施出境禁令”。
美国人权与学术自由组织在联合声明中，对于美国政府在针对中国的旅行建议中加入“D”标识表示赞赏。
资料照片：在中国遭“非法拘押”的美籍缅甸裔学者敏辛(Min Zin)和妻子西尔维娅·辛(Sylvia Zin)，及女儿素(Suu)的合影。(2026年2月，照片由西尔维亚提供)
联合声明还敦促唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统将促成敏辛的获释列为当务之急。
其它建议措施还包括将中国的旅行建议级别提升至第3级，即“重新考虑旅行”(Reconsider travel)，并附有“D”标识，以及将中国整体列入“支持非法拘押的国家”(State Sponsor of Wrongful Detention)名单。
联合声明提出，11月18日至19日中国深圳将举行亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会，12月14日至15日佛罗里达州多拉尔(Doral)将举行二十国集团(G-20)领导人峰会，相关决议若能在两个峰会之前通过，特朗普总统将获得强有力的国会授权，有助于他在与中国国家主席习近平会晤时，争取让敏辛获释。
这份联合声明由致力于救援海外被扣押美国公民的非盈利组织弗利基金会牵头，参与签署的还包括自由之家(Freedom House)、兰托斯人权与正义基金会(Lantos Foundation for Human Rights & Justice)以及学者风险网络(Scholars at Risk)等七家组织。
弗利基金会执行董事本杰明·格雷(Benjamin Gray) 在书面回复美国之音的置评请求时表示，第119届国会接近尾声，议程十分紧凑，但参议院第865号决议案和众议院第1549号决议案本身并无争议。
格雷告诉美国之音：“若能在这一期间以口头表决方式进行审议，它们(两项决议案)有望迅速获得通过。”
对于联合声明中提到的升级中国旅行建议以及把中国列为“支持非法拘押的国家”等具体措施，格雷表示，中国政府对于国会决议案或美国政府调整旅行建议等可能引发负面关注的举动非常敏感。
对于特朗普总统在接下来的两次美中领导人峰会中、再次谈及美国公民的非法拘押议题，格雷持乐观态度。他告诉美国之音：“我们预计，近期旅行建议的调整，以及我们所倡导的各项措施，将促使非法拘押美国人的议题，在未来习近平与特朗普计划进行的接触中，被列为议程的重中之重。”
敏辛是一名研究缅甸政治及中缅关系的美国学者。今年6月，他应邀赴云南参加学术会议后被中国当局拘押。北京方面指控他涉嫌从事危害中国国家安全的间谍活动。美国国务院8月20日认定敏辛遭到非法拘押。
特朗普总统9月30日曾公开透露，他一星期前与访美的习近平会晤时，谈到被中国拘押的美国公民和中国政治犯的问题。特朗普当时对记者表示：“我和习近平主席谈过，确实谈过。”
特朗普还补充道：“我们进行了交谈，我认为我们进行了一些非常、非常重要的讨论。希望这些讨论能取得成果。”
美国国务院9月30日也跟美国之音确认了相关消息。国务院发言人告诉美国之音：“特朗普政府致力于促成陈友麟(Youlin Chen))、敏辛以及所有在海外遭非法拘押的美国人获释。美国已直接向中国提出敏辛和陈博士的案件，呼吁立即释放他们。”
陈友麟是华裔美国地震学者，他2024年在北京机场准备返美时被捕，目前面临间谍罪指控。美国国务院今年3月认定他在中国遭到非法拘押。
北京此前一直否认有关中国政府进行“非法拘押”或“错误羁押”的说法，并表示中国司法机关依法办案。

要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
图片仅供说明之用。来源：Unsplash
中新社台北 11 月 10 日电 中国民航局 (CAA) 周二表示，台湾将从 12 月 1 日起禁止在航班上使用加热烟草产品，处罚包括最高五年监禁或最高 15 万新台币（4,564 美元）的罚款。
CAA 表示，这一变化旨在遵守《烟草危害预防法》，并解决与新型烟草和尼古丁产品（包括电子烟​​和加热烟草产品）相关的潜在安全风险。
该机构表示，使用此类产品可能会造成火灾和烟雾危险，并增加飞机维护成本。
根据修订后的规则，乘客将被禁止在飞行过程中的任何时候使用加热烟草产品，而现有的电子烟禁令将继续存在。
根据民航法，违法者最高可处五年以下有期徒刑、拘役或科新台币十五万元以下罚金。
如果违法行为导致死亡，犯罪者可能面临无期徒刑或至少七年的监禁。如果造成严重伤害，将被处以3至10年监禁。
民航局建议乘客在登机前查看航空公司网站或值机柜台的相关规定。
该机构表示，登机后，乘客应关闭电子烟、加热烟草装置以及相关设备和配件，并在整个飞行过程中避免使用它们。

Image for illustrative purposes only. Source: Unsplash
Taipei, Nov. 10 (CNA) Taiwan will ban the use of heated tobacco products on flights starting Dec. 1, with penalties including up to five years in prison or a fine of up to NT$150,000 (US$4,564), the Civil Aviation Administration (CAA) said Tuesday.
The CAA said the change was intended to comply with the Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act and address potential safety risks associated with newer tobacco and nicotine products, including e-cigarettes and heated tobacco products.
Using such products could create fire and smoke hazards and increase aircraft maintenance costs, the agency said.
Under the revised rules, passengers will be prohibited from using heated tobacco products at any point during a flight, while the existing ban on e-cigarettes will remain in place.
Violators could face up to five years in prison, detention or a fine of up to NT$150,000 under the Civil Aviation Act.
If a violation results in death, the offender could face life imprisonment or a prison term of at least seven years. If it causes serious injury, the penalty is three to 10 years in prison.
The CAA advised passengers to check the relevant rules on their airline's website or at check-in counters before boarding.
Once on board, passengers should keep e-cigarettes, heated tobacco devices and associated devices and accessories switched off and refrain from using them throughout the flight, the agency said.

台湾将公共资助流感药物的使用期限延长至 11 月 30 日

疾控中心发言人林明正（中）。中央通讯社照片2026年11月10日
中新社台北11月10日电 台湾疾病预防控制中心(CDC)周二表示，尽管流感感染人数有所下降，但疫情仍在持续，从11月15日到11月30日，将继续允许更多人获得公共资助的流感抗病毒药物。
根据疾病预防控制中心 10 月份发布的新闻稿，根据这项措施，指定的流感高风险人群中出现流感样症状的人可以获得公共资助的抗病毒药物。
符合条件的人群包括医疗机构的感染控制人员、长期护理机构的居民和工作人员、托儿工作者和保姆以及从学前班到高中的学生。
该措施还涵盖与重症流感高危人群共同生活或照顾的人员、畜禽养殖场工作人员、动物园工作人员和兽医检疫人员。
疾病预防控制中心此前曾两次延长更广泛的资格规则。
疾控中心发言人林明诚在例行新闻发布会上表示，流感活动已连续七周下降，截至上周已连续两周低于流感流行水平。
不过，他表示，由于严重病例数量持续居高不下，并且担心这样的宣布可能会向公众发出误导信息，因此疾病预防控制中心决定不宣布流感疫情结束。
根据CDC数据，上周门诊和急诊室因流感类疾病就诊的人数为91,879人，比前一周下降6.4%。
CDC表示，尽管有所下降，但上周仍报告新增103例重症病例和38例死亡，使自10月1日以来当前流感季节的累计病例总数达到645例重症病例和124例死亡。
重症病例中，69.9%为65岁以上人群，85.1%为患有基础慢性病的患者。
此外，据美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 称，97.1% 的重症病例涉及本季未接种流感疫苗的人。
林敦促有资格接种公费流感疫苗的人尽快接种疫苗，并采取预防措施，降低感染风险。
CDC 表示，自 10 月 1 日公共资助的疫苗接种计划开始以来，截至 11 月 4 日，已有超过 550 万人接种了流感疫苗。
与此同时，据美国疾病控制和预防中心 (CDC) 称，10 月中旬，台湾的 COVID-19 活动降至流行阈值以下，感染人数持续下降。
该机构表示，10 月 1 日至 11 月 4 日期间，共有 161 万人接种了 COVID-19 疫苗。

Taiwan extends expanded access to publicly funded flu drugs to Nov. 30
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
CDC spokesperson Lin Ming-cheng (center). CNA photo Nov. 10, 2026
Taipei, Nov. 10 (CNA) Taiwan's Centers for Disease Control (CDC) said Tuesday it would continue allowing more people to receive publicly funded flu antiviral drugs from Nov. 15 to Nov. 30, citing continued epidemic levels despite a decline in flu infections.
Under the measure, people in designated groups at higher risk of influenza who develop flu-like symptoms can receive publicly funded antiviral drugs, according to a CDC news release issued in October.
Eligible groups include infection-control personnel at medical institutions, residents and staff of long-term care facilities, childcare workers and nannies, and students from preschool through senior high school.
The measure also covers people living with or caring for individuals at high risk of severe influenza, livestock and poultry farm workers, zoo personnel, and veterinary quarantine personnel.
The CDC had extended the broader eligibility rules twice before.
CDC spokesperson Lin Ming-cheng (林明誠) said at a regular news conference that flu activity had declined for seven consecutive weeks and had been below the level used to define a flu epidemic for two consecutive weeks as of last week.
However, the CDC had decided not to declare an end to the flu epidemic because of the continued high number of severe cases and concerns that such an announcement could send a misleading message to the public, he said.
According to CDC data, 91,879 people sought medical attention for influenza-like illnesses at outpatient clinics and emergency rooms last week, down 6.4 percent from the previous week.
Despite the decline, 103 new severe cases and 38 deaths were reported last week, bringing the cumulative totals for the current flu season to 645 severe cases and 124 deaths since Oct. 1, the CDC said.
Of the severe cases, 69.9 percent involved people aged 65 or older, while 85.1 percent involved patients with underlying chronic conditions.
In addition, 97.1 percent of severe cases involved people who had not received a flu vaccination for this season, according to the CDC.
Lin urged people eligible for publicly funded flu vaccines to get vaccinated as soon as possible and take precautions to reduce their risk of infection.
As of Nov. 4, more than 5.5 million people had received flu vaccinations since the publicly funded vaccination program began on Oct. 1, the CDC said.
Meanwhile, COVID-19 activity in Taiwan fell below the epidemic threshold in mid-October, and infections have continued to decline, according to the CDC.
A total of 1.61 million people received COVID-19 vaccinations between Oct. 1 and Nov. 4, the agency said.

宝可梦珍稀邮票吸引游客参观台北世界邮票展
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
周二，中华邮政董事长王国材（左四）和其他官员在台北举行的新闻发布会上合影留念。中央通讯社照片2026年11月9日
中新社台北11月10日电 组织者周一表示，即将在台北举行的2026年菲律宾世界邮票锦标赛展览中，一张被称为“倒置珍妮”的罕见印刷错误美国邮票将成为亮点之一，而神奇宝贝主题邮票和商品在网上预售中大部分已售罄。
“倒置的珍妮”是 1918 年发行的著名的 24 美分美国邮票。它的图案是一架绰号“珍妮”的柯蒂斯 JN-4 双翼飞机，由于印刷错误，它被倒置在红框内。
据台湾国营邮政机构中华邮政股份有限公司称，全球仅存约 100 枚印刷错误的邮票。
根据拍卖记录，其中一枚在 2023 年 11 月的罗伯特·A·西格尔 (Robert A. Siegel) 拍卖会上以 200 万美元的价格售出，创下了单张美国邮票的拍卖纪录。
PHILATAIPEI 2026展览将于11月20日至25日在台北世界贸易中心举行，免费入场。
中华邮政在周一的新闻发布会上表示，此次展览以“创新无穷永续”为主题，将设有多个展区，包括珍稀邮票和故宫博物院专区、台湾与全球专题专区、邮票艺术DIY专区以及中华邮政130周年纪念专区。
中华邮政表示，此次活动将汇集来自69个国家和地区的邮政服务、邮票经销商和集邮爱好者，2,054个框架展示来自台湾和海外的稀有邮票收藏。
中华邮政董事长王国材表示，台湾上次举办世界集邮展览是在2016年，并补充说，他希望今年的活动有助于提升台湾的国际形象。
据中华邮政介绍，此次展出的其他历史邮票还包括1949年上海印制的《雁行基本邮票》、1911年的《阿根廷农民和旭日邮票》以及1888年的《龙马邮票》。
该公司表示，为期六天的展览还将举办日常活动，包括表演、签名会、讲座和神奇宝贝见面会活动。
周一，台北会场的货架上陈列着邮票和与神奇宝贝的联名商品。中央通讯社照片2026年11月9日
为了这次展览，中华邮政与神奇宝贝系列合作发行邮票和联名商品。
该公司周一表示，分配给在线预售的神奇宝贝主题邮票和商品占总数的60%，包括18万张邮票，大部分在两个小时内售罄。
王表示，由于合同限制，神奇宝贝商品不会补货。
据中华邮报报道，另有20%的神奇宝贝主题邮票和商品将于展览开幕当天上午1​​1点在台北世贸中心8号入口发售。另外20%的主题邮票将在中华邮政指定分店发售。
该公司表示，每位游客只会收到一张排队门票，且购买数量受每人限制。

Pokémon, rare stamps to draw visitors to Taipei world stamp exhibit
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Chunghwa Post Chairman Wang Kwo-tsai (fourth left) and other officials pose for a photo at a press event in Taipei on Tuesday. CNA photo Nov. 9, 2026
Taipei, Nov. 10 (CNA) A rare misprinted U.S. postage stamp known as the "Inverted Jenny" will be among the highlights of the upcoming PHILATAIPEI 2026 World Stamp Championship Exhibition in Taipei, while Pokémon-themed stamps and merchandise have mostly sold out in online presales, organizers said Monday.
The "Inverted Jenny" is a famous 24-cent U.S. postage stamp issued in 1918. It features a Curtiss JN-4 biplane, nicknamed the "Jenny," printed upside down within a red frame because of a printing error.
Only about 100 examples of the misprinted stamp were reportedly still in existence worldwide, according to Chunghwa Post Co., Ltd., Taiwan's state-run postal service.
One example sold for US$2 million at a Robert A. Siegel auction in November 2023, setting a record for a single U.S. stamp sold at auction, according to auction records.
The PHILATAIPEI 2026 exhibition will run from Nov. 20 to 25 at the Taipei World Trade Center, with free admission.
At a press conference on Monday, Chunghwa Post said the exhibition, themed "Innovation ∞ Sustainability," will feature several sections, including one dedicated to rare stamps and the National Palace Museum, a Taiwan and global thematic section, a stamp art DIY section, and a section marking Chunghwa Post's 130th anniversary.
The event will bring together postal services, stamp dealers and philatelists from 69 countries and territories, with 2,054 frames displaying rare stamp collections from Taiwan and abroad, Chunghwa Post said.
Chunghwa Post Chairman Wang Kwo-tsai (王國材) said Taiwan last hosted a world stamp exhibition in 2016, adding that he hoped this year's event would help raise Taiwan's international profile.
Other historical stamps on display will include the Shanghai-printed Flying Geese Basic Stamps from 1949, Argentina's Farmer and Rising Sun Stamp from 1911 and the Dragon-Horse Postage Stamps from 1888, according to Chunghwa Post.
The six-day exhibition will also feature daily activities, including performances, autograph sessions, lectures and Pokémon meet-and-greet events, the company said.
Stamps and co-branded merchandise with Pokémon are displayed on the shelves at the venue in Taipei on Monday. CNA photo Nov. 9, 2026
For the exhibition, Chunghwa Post has teamed up with the Pokémon franchise to release stamps and co-branded merchandise.
The company said Monday that the Pokémon-themed stamps and merchandise allocated to online presales, accounting for 60 percent of the total and including 180,000 stamps, sold out mostly within two hours.
Wang said the Pokémon merchandise would not be restocked because of contractual restrictions.
Another 20 percent of the Pokémon-themed stamps and merchandise will go on sale at 11 a.m. on the exhibition's opening day at Entrance 8 of the Taipei World Trade Center, according to Chunghwa Post. A further 20 percent of the themed stamps will be sold at designated Chunghwa Post branches.
Each visitor will receive only one queue ticket, and purchases will be subject to per-person limits, the company said.

summary: 中国对台北医学大会没有重大压力：组织者 - 聚焦台湾 中国对台北医学大会没有重大压力：组织者 要激活文本转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。即将举行的第 38 届世界内科医学大会的关键人物张善全医生（左三）和蔡丹尼尔（右一）周二在台北举行的新闻发布会上与其他医疗专业人士合影。 CNA 照片 2026 年 11 月 10 日 台北，11 月 10 日（中央通讯社）定于今年在台北举行的国际医学大会的组织者
content:
组织者：中国对台北医学大会没有重大压力 - 聚焦台湾
台北医学大会主办方：中国并未施加重大压力
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
即将举行的第 38 届世界内科医学大会的关键人物张善全医生（左三）和蔡丹尼尔（右一）周二在台北举行的新闻发布会上与其他医疗专业人士合影。中央通讯社照片2026年11月10日
中新社台北11月10日电 会议主席周二表示，定于本周在台北举行的国际医学大会的组织者在申办过程或筹备过程中没有面临来自中国的重大政治干预或压力。
第38届世界内科大会主席张上淳在台大医院新闻发布会上表示，台湾在四年前通过申办获得了主办权。
张说，台湾提交的投标书强调了其相对于其他国家的竞争投标的优势。
在被中央社问及组织者是否面临来自北京的压力时，张表示，国际内科医学会（ISIM）理事会对竞标进行了投票，最终选择台湾主办这次大会。
“基本上，我们没有面临太多的政治干扰……在整个筹备过程中，我们也没有感受到任何特别的压力，”台大医学院内科特聘教授张说。
台湾长期以来在参与国际组织方面面临来自中国的压力，包括每年一度的世界卫生组织（WHO）决策机构世界卫生大会（WHA）。
台湾曾于2009年至2016年以“中华台北”名义以观察员身份参加世界卫生大会，但自2017年以来，由于北京方面的反对，台湾一直没有被邀请回来，北京坚持台湾参与国际组织必须遵守“一个中国”原则。
同时担任 ISIM 理事会成员的张表示，已有 3,000 多人注册参加此次大会，其中包括来自台湾以外 60 个国家/地区的医生。
然而，张说，截至周二，还没有来自中国的与会者注册参加这次大会。
根据ISIM的官方网站，主办今年大会的台湾内科学会和中华内科学会都是会员组织，分别于1996年和2008年加入。
关于邀请，张表示，组织者没有直接邀请个别国家或医疗组织。
他说，有关大会的信息通过 ISIM 分发给所有会员组织，而台湾代表也在 2024 年布拉格举行的上一届大会上宣传了该活动。
关注人工智能、医学伦理
11 月 12 日至 15 日的大会将于台北南港展览中心举行，这标志着该活动自 2006 年以来首次重返台湾。
大会以“人工智能、医学和人类走向未来”为主题，将重点讨论人工智能（AI）在医疗保健领域的应用和伦理影响。
其中一个亮点将是对拟议的“人工智能、医疗保健和人文台北宣言”的讨论，该宣言概述了涵盖以人为本的护理、专业责任等方面的 14 条原则

No major Chinese pressure over Taipei medical congress: Organizers - Focus Taiwan
No major Chinese pressure over Taipei medical congress: Organizers
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Physicians Chang Shan-chwen (third left) and Daniel Tsai (first right), both key figures in the upcoming 38th World Congress of Internal Medicine, pose with other medical professionals at a press conference in Taipei on Tuesday. CNA photo Nov. 10, 2026
Taipei, Nov. 10 (CNA) Organizers of an international medical congress scheduled to take place in Taipei this week faced no significant political interference or pressure from China during the bidding process or preparations, the congress president said Tuesday.
Speaking at a press conference at National Taiwan University Hospital (NTUH), Chang Shan-chwen (張上淳), president of the 38th World Congress of Internal Medicine (WCIM), said Taiwan secured the right to host the event four years ago following a bidding process.
Chang said that Taiwan submitted a bid highlighting its strengths against competing bids from other countries.
Asked by CNA whether organizers had faced pressure from Beijing, Chang said the governing board of the International Society of Internal Medicine (ISIM) voted on the competing bids and ultimately selected Taiwan to host the congress.
"Basically, we did not face much political interference ... We also did not feel any particular pressure throughout the preparations," said Chang, a distinguished professor in the Department of Internal Medicine at National Taiwan University College of Medicine.
Taiwan has long faced pressure from China over its participation in international organizations, including the annual World Health Assembly (WHA), the decision-making body of the World Health Organization (WHO).
Taiwan attended the WHA as an observer under the name "Chinese Taipei" from 2009 to 2016 but has not been invited back since 2017 because of opposition from Beijing, which insists that Taiwan's participation in international organizations must adhere to its "one China" principle.
Chang, who also serves on ISIM's governing board, said more than 3,000 people had registered for the congress, including physicians from 60 countries outside Taiwan.
However, no participants from China had registered for the congress as of Tuesday, Chang said.
According to ISIM's official website, both the Taiwan Society of Internal Medicine -- which is organizing this year's congress -- and the Chinese Society of Internal Medicine are member organizations, having joined in 1996 and 2008, respectively.
Regarding invitations, Chang said organizers had not invited individual countries or medical organizations directly.
Instead, information about the congress was distributed to all member organizations through ISIM, while Taiwanese representatives also promoted the event at the previous congress in Prague in 2024, he said.
Focus on AI, medical ethics
The Nov. 12-15 congress, to be held at Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center, marks the event's return to Taiwan for the first time since 2006.
Under the theme "AI, Medicine, and Humanity into the Future," the congress will focus on the applications and ethical implications of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare.
One highlight will be discussions on a proposed "Taipei Declaration on Artificial Intelligence, Healthcare, and the Humanities," which outlines 14 principles covering human-centered care, professional accountability, patient safety, data governance and global health equity.
Daniel Tsai (蔡甫昌), director of NTUH's Ethics Center, said the draft had been circulated among international medical experts for feedback and would be discussed at a forum on Nov. 13.
Organizers hope to finalize and release the declaration afterward.

台湾与巴拉圭新领导人接触；关系稳定：外交部

巴拉圭新任总统佩德罗·阿利亚纳。照片：路透社
中新社台北11月10日电 外交部周二表示，台湾与巴拉圭新任总统佩德罗·阿利亚纳保持着密切联系，尽管前任总统被弹劾并罢免，但两国关系仍保持密切和友好。
外交部发言人萧光伟也表示，台湾与巴拉圭的合作项目正在按计划进行，并未受到南美国家上野银行倒闭的影响。
前总统圣地亚哥·佩纳因涉嫌卷入导致上野银行倒闭的丑闻而被弹劾并免职后，当被问及台湾与巴拉圭新政府的关系时，萧表示。
佩纳于 2023 年 8 月就任总统，被誉为台湾与台湾建交的坚定支持者。周五，在数字银行倒闭后，跨党派议员一致投票弹劾他，他被免职，他们称这家数字银行与他的私人商业利益有关。
佩纳曾提出辞职，但在该银行倒闭引发危机，导致该国一半以上人口无法访问其账户后，议员们投票弹劾他并指控他行为不当。
他的副手阿丽安娜随后宣誓就任该国新总统。
佩尼亚直到去年才持有该银行所属公司的股份，他否认有任何不当行为。
萧在周二的外交部每周新闻发布会上表示，台湾驻巴拉圭大使李岳融已转达台湾对阿利亚纳就任总统的祝贺，双方同意继续现有的合作项目。
萧表示，阿利亚纳长期以来与台湾保持着密切和亲切的关系，包括在担任巴拉圭众议院议长期间和担任副总统之前。
萧说，阿利亚纳也多次公开重申台湾是巴拉圭的重要战略盟友。
外交部发言人还证实巴拉圭媒体周一发表的报道称，阿利亚纳计划于本月晚些时候以副总统身份访问台湾。
不过，萧表示，鉴于巴拉圭国内局势，此次访问将被推迟。
萧表示，外交部将邀请阿丽安娜稍后访问台湾。

Taiwan in contact with Paraguay's new leader; ties stable: MOFA
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Paraguay's new President Pedro Alliana. Photo: Reuters
Taipei, Nov. 10 (CNA) Taiwan has been in close contact with Paraguay's new President Pedro Alliana, and relations between the two countries remain close and cordial despite the impeachment and removal of his predecessor from office, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) said Tuesday.
MOFA spokesman Hsiao Kuangwei (蕭光偉) also said that Taiwan's cooperation projects with Paraguay were proceeding as planned and had not been affected by the collapse of the South American country's Ueno Bank.
Hsiao made the remarks when asked about Taiwan's relations with Paraguay's new administration following the impeachment and removal of former President Santiago Peña over his alleged role in a scandal that led to the collapse of Ueno Bank.
Peña assumed the presidency in August 2023 and was known as a staunch supporter of his country's diplomatic ties with Taiwan. He was removed from office on Friday after lawmakers across party lines voted unanimously to impeach him, following the collapse of the digital bank, which they said had links to his private business interests.
Peña had offered to resign, but lawmakers instead voted to impeach him and charged him with misconduct, after the bank's collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.
His deputy, Alliana, was subsequently sworn in as the country's new president.
Peña, who held shares in the company that owned the bank until last year, has denied any wrongdoing.
Speaking at MOFA's weekly news briefing Tuesday, Hsiao said Taiwan's ambassador to Paraguay, Iván Lee (李岳融), had conveyed Taiwan's congratulations to Alliana on his assumption of the presidency and that both sides had agreed to continue their existing cooperation projects.
Hsiao said Alliana had maintained close and cordial relations with Taiwan for a long time, including during his tenure as president of Paraguay's Chamber of Deputies, before becoming vice president.
Alliana has also repeatedly reaffirmed publicly that Taiwan is an important strategic ally of Paraguay, Hsiao said.
The MOFA spokesman also confirmed a Paraguayan media report published Monday that Alliana had been scheduled to visit Taiwan later this month in his capacity as vice president.
The visit would, however, be postponed in light of the domestic situation in Paraguay, Hsiao said.
MOFA would extend an invitation to Alliana to visit Taiwan at a later date, Hsiao said.

中新社台北11月10日电 立陶宛一家媒体周一报道，欧洲国家政府已要求更改其驻立陶宛代表处的名称，以改善双边关系，台湾周二重申，没有计划更改驻立陶宛代表处的名称。
“该办公室的名称是为了深化双边关系而选择的，目前没有计划改变它，”外交部副部长陈明琪周二在立法会议期间告诉记者。
与此同时，外交部发言人萧光伟表示，外交部对立陶宛媒体的报道或“报告中有关双边关系的猜测”“不予置评”。
萧在外交部每周新闻发布会上表示：“不过，我们想重申，台湾驻立陶宛代表处的名称是台湾和立陶宛政府经过认真协商达成共识的结果。”
据称，波罗的海国家于九月下旬提出要求，要求驻维尔纽斯台北办事处在一周内更改名称。
立陶宛公共广播公司LRT周一援引当地新闻网站Delfi报道称，外交部副部长维德曼塔斯·维比克斯和外交官里卡达斯·斯莱帕维丘斯于9月24日会见了台湾驻立陶宛首席特使王雪虹，讨论了双边关系相关问题。
德尔菲说，据报道，在会议期间，立陶宛官员向王提交了一份非官方文件，要求在中国国庆节 10 月 1 日之前更改该办公室的名称。
据德尔菲报告称，该文件称，该办公室目前的名称“阻碍立陶宛与台湾之间经济关系的发展，给企业造成困难”。
LRT 周一援引立陶宛外交部长 Kęstutis Budrys 的回应称，该信息“报道不准确”，但他拒绝进一步置评。
台湾驻立陶宛代表处于2021年11月18日在维尔纽斯成立，立陶宛驻台北贸易代表处于2022年11月7日正式开业。
台湾在海外的代表处通常被命名为“台北经济文化办事处”或“台北代表处”，以符合东道国的偏好，以避免暗示台湾是与中国分离的国家。

Taiwan will not rename representative office in Lithuania: Deputy FM - Focus Taiwan
Taiwan will not rename representative office in Lithuania: Deputy FM
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 10 (CNA) Taiwan reiterated Tuesday that it has no plans to change the name of its representative office in Lithuania, after a Lithuanian media outlet reported on Monday that the government of the European country had requested such a change in a bid to improve bilateral ties.
"The name of the office was chosen with the goal of deepening bilateral ties, and there are currently no plans to change it," Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi (陳明祺) told reporters Tuesday on the sidelines of a legislative session.
Meanwhile, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) spokesperson Hsiao Kuangwei (蕭光偉) said MOFA had "no comment" on the Lithuanian media report or the "speculations made in the report" concerning bilateral relations.
"However, we wish to reiterate that the name, the Taiwanese Representative Office in Lithuania, was decided as a result of consensus reached through careful consultation between the governments of Taiwan and Lithuania," Hsiao said at MOFA's weekly press briefing.
Chen and Hsiao made their respective remarks in response to questions about the reported request, which was allegedly made by the Baltic state in late September, asking the Taipei office in Vilnius to change its name within a week.
Lithuania's public broadcaster LRT on Monday cited local news website Delfi as reporting that Deputy Foreign Minister Vidmantas Verbickas and diplomat Ričardas Šlepavičius had met with Taiwan's top envoy to Lithuania, Constance Wang (王雪虹), on Sept. 24 to discuss issues related to bilateral relations.
During the meeting, the Lithuanian officials reportedly presented Wang with an unofficial document requesting that the office's name be changed by Oct. 1, China's National Day, Delfi said.
The document argued that the office's current name was "obstructing the development of economic ties between Lithuania and Taiwan and creating difficulties for businesses," according to the Delfi report.
In response, Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys was quoted by LRT on Monday as saying that the information had been "inaccurately reported," and he declined to comment further.
The Taiwanese Representative Office in Lithuania was opened in Vilnius on Nov. 18, 2021, while the Lithuanian Trade Representative Office in Taipei was officially opened on Nov. 7, 2022.
Taiwan's representative offices overseas are typically named "Taipei Economic and Cultural Office" or "Taipei Representative Office," in keeping with host countries' preferences to avoid references that could imply Taiwan is a separate country from China.
Beijing, which considers Taiwan part of the same country, has sought to impose political and economic penalties on Lithuania over its decision to include the word "Taiwanese" in the name of Taiwan's office.
Beijing's punitive measures have included recalling its ambassador to Lithuania, downgrading diplomatic relations with the Baltic state, expelling Lithuania's ambassador to China, and suspending some bilateral trade.
With a new government having taken office, Lithuania has been seeking to improve ties with Beijing. Since then, there have been repeated media reports that Vilnius has asked Taipei to change the name of its representative office.
Taipei, however, has repeatedly said it has no intention of doing so.

# 法国指责上个月针对超市冷藏设备的网络攻击是伊朗干的， 伊朗拒绝法国的指控

伊朗 –  法国指责说，上个月针对超市冷藏设备的网络攻击是伊朗干的。 伊朗周二表示，这种说法是“毫无根据的”。

发表时间： 10/11/2026 - 22:34

 3 分钟 浏览时间

 法国外长巴罗 AFP - LUDOVIC MARIN

 作者： [安东尼](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%9C%E5%B0%BC/ "安东尼")

广告

继续浏览后续

10月11日至12日发生的网络攻击波及了法国数百家超市，导致法国冷藏和冷冻设备温度升高，迫使许多超市不得不丢弃库存中所有易腐食品。

11月初，欧洲至少另外11个国家也报告了类似事件。

法国外交部长巴罗周二表示，除了召见伊朗大使并寻求在欧洲层面实施制裁外，法国“不排除任何可能性，并将采取一切必要且适度的措施——包括那些我们可能不会公开披露的措施——以阻止任何进一步的攻击”。

法新社报道，伊朗说： 法国提出这些指控，不过是“将其自身的治理失误转嫁到他人身上”。

与此同时，德黑兰方面表示，面对“非法的外国活动”，伊朗将“毫不犹豫地采取必要且适当的措施，以维护其国家利益和安全”。

伊朗外交部在一份声明中表示：“伊朗外交部断然拒绝法国政府针对伊朗所提出的毫无根据且片面的指控，这些指控涉及所谓的在法国发生的网络活动。”

声明还称，伊朗“强烈谴责这种针对伊朗伊斯兰共和国进行指责的老套做法”。

2026 年 11 月 10 日，在与可能弹劾国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 相关的程序性投票之前，一名孤独的抗议者在美国国会大厦前举着“弹劾赫格斯”的牌子。（乔纳森·恩斯特/路透社）
众议院周二晚上投票决定将针对国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯的弹劾条款提交给众议院司法委员会，从而有效地驳回了罢免赫格塞斯内阁职务的努力。
众议院共和党人以 211 比 204 票否决了肯塔基州共和党众议员托马斯·马西提出的弹劾赫格斯塞斯的提议。马西指控赫格赛斯在处理加勒比和太平洋地区的缉毒行动和法外处决过程中疏忽大意，并进行了非法活动； 2月份未经国会批准袭击伊朗；对亚利桑那州民主党参议员马克·凯利（Mark Kelly）进行报复，因为这位资深议员根据非法命令向部队发表了言论；在未宣战的情况下俘获委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗；及其他操作。
文章称，“国防部长彼得·赫格斯的这种行为表明，如果允许他继续留任，他将仍然对宪法构成威胁，而且他的行为方式与他的职责和法治严重不相容。”
将这些条款发送给司法委员会的决定可能会将投票推迟到一月份，届时民主党将在国会占据多数席位。
截至周四，民主党在众议院赢得了 256 个席位，共和党赢得了 168 个席位，而在参议院，民主党至少拥有 54 个席位，而共和党则拥有 44 个席位。
如果众议院明年投票弹劾赫格塞斯，则任何条款都需要三分之二多数才能迫使赫格塞斯下台。
在周二早上投票前举行的一次罕见的新闻发布会上，赫格斯称马西为“心怀不满和失败的国会议员”，试图“损害这位总统、这个国家，以及最不负责任的捍卫国家的战士”。
赫格塞斯指出，唐纳德·特朗普总统曾两次被弹劾，但并未被定罪，他表示，他将“一周中的每一天都接管这家公司”。
“这些决议是一场闹剧。他们嘲笑宪法。他们攻击指挥系统，并将执行合法命令的战士定为犯罪，”赫格塞斯说。
特朗普表示，他将支持国防部长，周一称他“做得非常好”。
如果这一努力成功，这将标志着美国国防部长的第二次弹劾和内阁成员的第三次弹劾。 2024 年，国土安全部部长亚历杭德罗·马约卡斯因总统乔·拜登在美墨边境的移民政策而被弹劾。参议院在审判前投票驳回了这些指控。
1876 年，战争部长威廉·贝尔纳普 (William Belknap) 在辞职后不久就因腐败指控而遭到弹劾。后来他在参议院被无罪释放。
退伍军人倡导非营利组织 Common Defense 于 10 月发布的一项调查发现，军人及其家属对他们认为的武装部队政治化感到不安。

A lone protester holds an “Impeach Hegseth” sign on the grounds of the U.S. Capitol ahead of a procedural vote related to the potential impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Nov. 10, 2026. (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters)
The House voted Tuesday evening to send the proposed impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the House Judiciary Committee, effectively quashing an effort to oust Hegseth from his cabinet post.
In a 211 to 204 vote, House Republicans sidestepped an effort proposed by Republican Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky to impeach Hegseth. Massie charged that Hegseth was negligent and conducted illegal activity in his handling of counternarcotics operations and extrajudicial killings in the Caribbean and Pacific; attacking Iran in February without congressional approval; retaliating against Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., for the veteran lawmaker’s statements to troops on illegal orders; capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro without a declaration of war; and other operations.
“Secretary of Defense Peter Hegseth, by such conduct, has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law,” the articles stated.
The decision to send the articles to the Judiciary Committee likely delays the vote until January, when Democrats take over the majority in Congress.
As of Thursday, Democrats won 256 seats in the House to the Republicans’ 168, while in the Senate, Democrats have at least 54 seats to 44 Republican seats.
If the House votes to impeach Hegseth next year, a two-thirds majority would be needed on any of the articles to force Hegseth out of office.
In a rare news conference Tuesday morning before the vote, Hegseth called Massie a “disgruntled and defeated congressman” seeking to “do damage to this president, this country, and most irresponsibly, the warriors who defend it.”
Noting that President Donald Trump was impeached twice but not convicted, Hegseth said he would “take that company every day of the week.”
“These resolutions are a farce. They mock the Constitution. They attack the chain of command, and they criminalize the warfighters who execute lawful orders,” Hegseth said.
Trump has said he would stand by his defense secretary, saying Monday that he’s “done a very good job.”
If the effort had succeeded, it would have marked the second impeachment of a U.S. defense secretary and third of a cabinet member. In 2024, Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas was impeached over President Joe Biden’s immigration policies at the U.S.-Mexico border. The Senate voted to dismiss the charges before it went to trial.
Secretary of War William Belknap was impeached in 1876 on corruption charges shortly after he resigned. He was later acquitted in the Senate.
A survey released in October by the military-veterans advocacy non-profit Common Defense found that troops and family members are uncomfortable with what they see as the politicization of the armed forces.
According to the survey, conducted by Change Research, 54% of active-duty personnel surveyed disapproved of Hegseth, while 64% of military family members disapproved.
A majority of the group of 731 active-duty troops, veterans and military family members also believe decisions within the department were being made for political gain, and 53% of active-duty personnel said the politicization was making them want to leave the military sooner than anticipated.
Nearly half the active-duty personnel also said they oppose Operation Epic Fury, the United States’ operation against Iran.
Patricia Kime is a senior writer covering military and veterans health care, medicine and personnel issues.

Department of the Treasury Financial Crimes Enforcement Network
Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), Treasury.
FinCEN is issuing notice of an order, pursuant to section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act (Pub. L. 116-283), as amended by section 6106(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81), finding that MEXC Global—including any of its subsidiaries, branches, and offices, as well as any successor entities, operating in any jurisdiction outside of the United States—is a financial institution operating outside of the United States of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance and prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global.
This action is effective December 10, 2026.
FinCEN's Regulatory Support Section by submitting an inquiry at www.fincen.gov/​contact.
As set out in this order, MEXC Global has facilitated funds transfers by Russia-affiliated illicit actors and in connection with other Russia-associated illicit activities, including sanctions evasion, and activity facilitated by Russian darknet markets. It has also facilitated billions of dollars in transactions benefitting Iran and its proxies, financial facilitators of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), and other cybercrime actors. Accordingly, this order (1) sets forth FinCEN's determination that MEXC Global, a convertible virtual currency (CVC) exchanger, along with any subsidiaries, branches, and offices of MEXC Global, and any successor entities, operating in any jurisdiction outside of the United States (collectively, MEXC Global) [1] is a financial institution operating outside of the United States of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance; and (2) prohibits certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global, by any covered financial institution.
Section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act (Pub. L. 116-283), as amended by section 6106(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81) (section 9714),[2] provides, in relevant part, that, if the Secretary of the Treasury (Secretary) “determines that reasonable grounds exist for concluding that one or more financial institutions operating outside of the United States . . . is of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance,” the Secretary may, “by order, regulation, or otherwise as permitted by law”: (1) require domestic financial institutions and domestic financial agencies to take one or more of the special measures described in 31 U.S.C. 5318A(b); [3] or (2) prohibit, or impose conditions upon, certain transmittals of funds (as defined by the Secretary) by any domestic financial institution or domestic financial agency (collectively, covered financial institutions), if such transmittal of funds involves any such financial institution. The authority of the Secretary to administer both section 9714 and the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) has been delegated to FinCEN.[4]
Pursuant to section 9714, the Secretary may impose one or more of six special measures. First, the Secretary may impose any of the five special measures provided for in 31 U.S.C. 5318A(b), commonly known as section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act.[5] Through special measures one through four, the Secretary may impose additional recordkeeping, information collection, and reporting requirements on covered financial institutions.[6] Through special measure five, the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, and the Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, may “prohibit, or impose conditions upon, the opening or maintaining in the United States of a correspondent account or payable-through account” for or on behalf of a foreign banking institution, if such correspondent account or payable-through account involves the financial institution operating outside of the United States found to be of primary money laundering concern.[7] In addition ( printed page 72421) to the special measures set out in 31 U.S.C. 5318A, section 9714 also provides that the Secretary may impose a special measure prohibiting, or imposing conditions upon, certain transmittals of funds.[8]
MEXC Global is a CVC exchanger founded in 2018 that is incorporated in the Seychelles, without a virtual asset service provider license [9] and operates in and across over 170 countries [10] through an array of current or former subsidiaries, branches, and offices, including, but not limited to, MEXC Global Ltd and MX Global Ltd in Seychelles; MEXC Estonia OÜ in Estonia; GIDA Technology AG in Switzerland; MXC Global Ltd in the United Kingdom; and, formerly, Singapore-registered MEXC Global Foundation Ltd and MEXC Singapore Pte Ltd.[11]
As of June 2026, MEXC Global processed more than USD 1 billion in daily transactions, while maintaining approximately USD 5 billion in reserve assets. As such, MEXC Global is among the 20 largest CVC exchangers in the world by trading volume.[12] As of December 2025, MEXC Global commanded approximately nine percent of the global market share of centralized CVC exchangers by trading volume.[13] By comparison, the assets of the two largest centralized CVC exchangers together represented 47.4 percent of the global market share.[14]
According to its user agreement, MEXC Global allows customers to open user accounts for exchange between various fiat currencies and CVC, as well as for futures trading and other services.[15] And, according to non-public information available to FinCEN, as of July 2026, MEXC Global offers the ability to trade in over fifty currencies, including USD and Russian rubles (RUB), as well as access to over 3,000 different CVCs and tokenized assets.
III. Finding That MEXC Global Is a Financial Institution Operating Outside the United States That Is of Primary Money Laundering Concern in Connection With Russian Illicit Finance
Based on public and non-public information available to FinCEN, FinCEN finds that reasonable grounds exist for concluding that MEXC Global is a financial institution of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance—namely, through its facilitation of funds transfers by Russia-affiliated illicit actors and in connection with other Russia-associated illicit activities, including sanctions evasion, and activity facilitated by Russian darknet markets. Moreover, FinCEN assesses that, in addition to facilitating Russian illicit finance, MEXC Global has, in parallel, facilitated billions of dollars in transactions benefitting Iran and its proxies, financial facilitators of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), and other cybercrime actors.
In making this finding, FinCEN has considered the relevant evidence in light of factors identified in 31 U.S.C. 5318A(c)(2)(B), taking into account the specific circumstances of money laundering activities in connection with Russian illicit finance and the protection of U.S. national security and the U.S. financial system. While FinCEN is under no obligation pursuant to section 9714 to consider any particular factor or set of factors when making a finding that a financial institution operating outside of the United States is of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance, it nonetheless finds these factors instructive in guiding the analysis set forth below.[16]
A. MEXC Global Is a Financial Institution Operating Outside the United States
Although section 9714 does not expressly define the term “financial institution,” FinCEN has long defined that term to include “money transmitters,” including persons that accept and transmit value that substitutes for currency, such as CVC.[17] MEXC Global, in operating as a CVC exchanger, is a “money transmitter” because it is engaged in the transfer of funds or value that substitutes for currency.[18]
By its own account and as described above, MEXC Global operates through affiliates throughout the world—over time maintaining, for instance, subsidiaries, branches, and offices in Seychelles, Hong Kong, Singapore, Estonia, and the United Kingdom—and offers a range of money transmitter services for individual and institutional customers in the CVC sector in over 170 countries.[19] Considering the services that it provides and its places of registration, FinCEN assesses that MEXC Global is a financial institution operating outside of the United States within the meaning of section 9714.
Notably, to the extent that MEXC Global maintains or otherwise operates through affiliates, subsidiaries, branches, or offices in the United States, this order expressly excludes all such affiliates, subsidiaries, branches, or offices from the definition of “MEXC Global” and, accordingly, such affiliates, subsidiaries, branches, or offices are outside the scope of this order.
B. Finding That MEXC Global Is a Financial Institution of Primary Money Laundering Concern in Connection With Russian Illicit Finance
While MEXC Global's anti-money laundering and countering the financing ( printed page 72422) of terrorism (AML/CFT), customer identification and verification (sometimes referred to as “Know Your Customer” or “KYC” information), and other due diligence processes [20] prohibit, on paper, the opening of accounts by individuals in certain jurisdictions, FinCEN assesses that, based on public and non-public information, MEXC Global has facilitated transactions involving those prohibited jurisdictions. In addition, MEXC Global has facilitated transactions involving Russia-affiliated illicit actors and associated illicit activities, including sanctions evasion, and activity facilitated by Russian darknet markets, as well as transactions involving not only U.S.-, European Union-, and United Kingdom-sanctioned persons working on behalf of Iran and its proxies and the DPRK, but also an array of cybercrime actors.
Notwithstanding MEXC Global's AML/CFT and other due diligence processes, FinCEN found that MEXC Global has skirted compliance with applicable regulatory requirements [21] —multiple nations' financial regulators have issued notices highlighting that MEXC Global has operated in their jurisdictions without the proper license, and in at least one case added the CVC exchanger to a list of suspicious CVC trading platforms [22] —and, importantly, that, between May 2021 and May 2026, MEXC Global facilitated the movement of USD 16.7 billion in funds connected to Russian illicit finance and other illicit activities, including sanctions evasion and cybercrime, posing a significant threat to the U.S. financial system. Indeed, within those transactions, FinCEN identified numerous instances in which MEXC Global processed transactions in violation of its own user agreement, including direct transactions between MEXC Global and sanctioned actors, some of whom were operating from MEXC Global's list of prohibited jurisdictions.[23]
1. MEXC Global Is Used in Furtherance of Sanctions Evasion in Connection With Russian Illicit Finance
MEXC Global has a history of processing CVC transfers for multiple key actors that support Russian illicit finance. According to FinCEN analysis of blockchain data, between May 2021 and May 2026, MEXC Global sent or received nearly USD 1.5 billion in direct and indirect exposure to transactions linked to Russian sanctions evasion and had significant exposure to Russian cyber actors connected to sanctions evasion and/or cybercrime. This includes USD 232 million in direct transactions with entities sanctioned by the United States, the European Union (EU), and/or the United Kingdom (UK).[24] For example, MEXC Global transacted with the sanctioned, Russia-backed CVC exchangers Garantex and Grinex. Between 2019 and 2025, Garantex facilitated the movement of over USD 100 million for ransomware actors and other cybercriminals.[25] Garantex's successor entity, Grinex, is itself a vehicle for sanctions evasion, as it was created by Garantex employees to move funds after Garantex was designated by OFAC for operating in Russia's financial services sector.[26] Following these public designations, MEXC Global directly facilitated approximately USD 129 million in activity with Garantex and USD 4.1 million in activity with Grinex, and MEXC Global continued to transact with both entities as recently as June 2026. Similarly, MEXC Global transacted with components of the Russia-based A7 Network,[27] a self-described sanctions-resistant payment service provider created by the U.S.-, EU- and UK-designated Moldovan oligarch Ilan Shor [28] and Russia's state-owned defense bank Promsvyazbank Public Joint Stock Company (PSB),[29] that has evolved into a conduit for illicit activity associated with a wide range of threat actors, including the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and its Quds Force, DPRK-affiliated actors; ( printed page 72423) Iran-backed terrorist organizations; and cybercriminals and ransomware actors.[30] Significantly, OFAC has designated the founders and core components and enablers of the A7 Network, and recently designated the A7 Network, itself, as a significant transnational criminal organization.[31] Further, FinCEN recently found that transactions involving any company operating outside of the United States that is controlled by the A7 Network belong to a class of transactions of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance.[32] Based on analysis of blockchain data, FinCEN assesses that MEXC Global facilitated the transmission of at least USD 26 million benefitting the now sanctioned A7 Network and sent or received almost USD 200 million connected to the A7A5 token (a ruble-backed stablecoin that operates on the Tron and Ethereum blockchains [33] to transfer value across A7 Network-linked actors where banking channels are restricted or less dependable),[34] including its issuer Old Vector LLC and owner Ilan Shor, both sanctioned by OFAC, as well as the European Union and the United Kingdom.[35]
In addition, MEXC Global has repeatedly transacted with high-risk CVC exchangers that have been sanctioned or that allegedly have no customer identification verification requirements. For example, between May 2018 and July 2026, MEXC Global directly facilitated transactions cumulatively worth over USD 13 billion with at least four high-risk CVC exchangers sanctioned by the UK for facilitating Russian sanctions evasion and funding Russian military operations in Ukraine.[36] Between May 2021 and May 2026, it also processed approximately USD 2.9 billion in direct transactions with Russian and other CVC exchangers that allegedly do not collect customer identification and verification information, which poses a high risk of transacting with sanctioned entities and individuals and for otherwise engaging in illicit activity. In addition, between September 2020 and July 2026, MEXC Global facilitated USD 8.5 million in transactions involving Russian darknet markets that are known to facilitate the sale of illicit goods and services.
Based on MEXC Global's facilitation of transactions for sanctioned and high-risk Russian CVC exchangers, including the A7 Network, which are widely known to move funds for sanctioned actors, cybercriminals, and ransomware actors, FinCEN assesses that MEXC Global is a financial institution of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance.
2. MEXC Global Is Used in Furtherance of International Money Laundering
According to public and non-public information, MEXC Global also facilitates activity in furtherance of international money laundering in support of Iran and its proxies, financial facilitators of the DPRK, and cybercrime.
a. MEXC Global Facilitated Transactions Involving Iran and Its Proxies
According to FinCEN analysis of blockchain information, between May 2021 and May 2026, MEXC Global facilitated the transmission of nearly USD 2 billion connected to identified Iranian actors or known or suspected terrorist groups, including approximately USD 1.87 billion in transactions with exposure to Iran, a jurisdiction that is the subject of comprehensive U.S. sanctions [37] and special measures imposed by FinCEN pursuant to section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act (31 U.S.C. 5318A) which prohibit covered financial institutions from opening or maintaining correspondent accounts in the United States for, or on behalf of, Iranian financial institutions.[38] Despite the fact that MEXC Global's user agreement states that individuals and entities located in Iran are not allowed to use its platform, FinCEN assesses that over USD 1 billion of this exposure took the form of direct transactions between MEXC Global and more than 40 identified Iranian CVC exchangers, some of which are the subject of U.S. and international sanctions. Between May 2021 and May 2026, FinCEN assesses that MEXC Global also facilitated the transmission of approximately USD 22 million in transactions associated with the U.S.- and EU-sanctioned Central Bank of Iran and the U.S.-, EU-, and UK-sanctioned IRGC and its Quds Force.[39]
MEXC Global has also been exploited by multiple Iran proxy groups. For example, FinCEN identified approximately USD 36 million in transactions that occurred between May 2021 and May 2026 that went to or from MEXC Global related to the Gaza-based U.S.- and UK-sanctioned Al-Qassam Brigades and other Iran linked terrorist groups.[40]
b. MEXC Global Facilitated Transactions Involving Financial Facilitators of the DPRK
MEXC Global has also transmitted funds on behalf of a financial facilitator of the DPRK, a jurisdiction that, like Iran, is the subject of comprehensive U.S. sanctions [41] and special measures imposed by FinCEN that prohibit covered financial institutions from opening or maintaining correspondent accounts in the United States for, or on behalf of, DPRK financial institutions.[42] For instance, FinCEN assesses that MEXC Global facilitated U.S.-sanctioned DPRK money launderer Sim Hyon Sop's receipt of approximately USD 350,000 between June and September 2025, more than two years after Sop had been designated by OFAC and even though, as part of his April 2023 designation, OFAC specifically identified and sanctioned his CVC addresses.[43]
c. MEXC Global Facilitated Transactions Connected to Cybercrime
Finally, MEXC Global frequently processes transactions connected to cyber-enabled crimes, ranging from darknet marketplace activity (including the Russian darknet marketplace activity discussed above) and ransomware payments to scam proceeds and stolen funds. Between May 2021 and May 2026, FinCEN assesses that at least USD 1.99 billion in funds originating from or moving to illicit cyber actors moved through MEXC Global, an average of more than USD 1 million per day. Between January 2022 to July 2024, MEXC Global received more than USD 37.9 million in suspected ransomware payments, with exposure to over 125 ransomware variants. MEXC Global also hosts a particularly high-use ransomware-related deposit address, which received over USD 1.17 million during the same period.
C. The Extent to Which MEXC Global Is Used for Legitimate Business Purposes
In reaching its finding that MEXC Global is a financial institution operating outside the United States of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance, FinCEN considered the extent to which MEXC Global is used for legitimate business purposes.[44] As of June 2026, MEXC Global conducted USD 1 billion in daily transactions, putting it among the top 20 largest CVC exchangers in the world by trading volume. Although FinCEN does not have full insight into the scope of MEXC Global's legitimate activities, for the purposes of this action, FinCEN assumes that a portion of MEXC Global's business activities are legitimate. However, FinCEN assesses that since May 2021, MEXC Global has facilitated at least USD 16.7 billion in likely illicit activity. Accordingly, any legitimate business conducted by MEXC Global is outweighed by the risks posed by MEXC Global's facilitation of illicit activity, including sanctions evasion by Russia and Iran, and the need to protect the U.S. financial sector from the money laundering and terrorist financing risks presented by MEXC Global.
D. The Extent to Which This Action Would Guard Against International Money Laundering and Other Financial Crimes Associated With Russian Illicit Finance
A finding that MEXC Global is of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance establishes—and emphasizes—the significant illicit finance risks posed by MEXC Global's provision of financial services to the Russian illicit finance ecosystem, Russian and other darknet markets and high-risk exchanges. Further, notwithstanding MEXC Global's ties to Russian illicit finance, FinCEN assesses that it has facilitated over USD 1.87 billion in transactions with exposure to Iran, including over USD 1 billion in direct transactions between MEXC Global and Iranian CVC exchangers, as well as transactions benefiting the DPRK and an array of illicit cyber actors, each of which present significant risks to the U.S. financial system. Accordingly, this order will place U.S. and foreign financial institutions and regulators on notice to guard against those risks. Moreover, such a finding—in combination with a prohibition on certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global by covered financial institutions—will help safeguard the U.S. financial system by severing MEXC Global's access.
IV. Imposition of a Special Measure Prohibiting Certain Transmittals of Funds Involving MEXC Global
Having found that MEXC Global is a financial institution operating outside of the United States that is of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance, FinCEN has determined that the imposition of a special measure prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global is warranted.[45] In making this determination and assessing which special measures may be appropriate, FinCEN has considered the relevant evidence in light of factors identified in 31 U.S.C. 5318A(a)(4)(B). While FinCEN is under no obligation pursuant to section 9714 to consider any particular factor or set of factors in selecting one or more special measures, it nonetheless finds these factors instructive in guiding the analysis set forth below.[46]
A. Whether the Prohibition Would Address the Money Laundering Concern in a Manner Consistent With U.S. National Security and Foreign Policy Interests
FinCEN has considered the effect this action will have on U.S. national security and foreign policy, as well as the extent to which multilateral groups or other nations have taken similar actions.[47] FinCEN has found that, in addition to facilitating Russian illicit financial activity and sanctions evasion schemes and serving as a high-density transactional node for high-risk CVC exchangers, MEXC Global plays a broader role in facilitating transactions for a diverse range of transnational illicit actors. In particular, MEXC Global processes transactions connected to Iranian sanctions evasion, terrorist financing, and the laundering of scam and ransomware proceeds. FinCEN, therefore, assesses that imposing a prohibition on certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global is necessary to safeguard U.S. national security and the U.S. financial system, as well as to serve key U.S. national security objectives.
In light of the quantity and volume of transactions linked to known or suspected illicit activity processed through MEXC Global, prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global would insulate the U.S. financial system from money laundering and other financial crimes. In particular, prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global would further ongoing U.S. efforts to curtail suspected Russia-associated illicit activity and financial transactions. And, targeting illicit proceeds moved by sanctions evasion networks, especially those with a nexus to Iran, is of highest priority for the United States. Consequently, prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global will serve the U.S. national security and foreign policy interests by protecting the U.S. and international financial system from known threat actors.
Moreover, this action reinforces the expectations of AML/CFT compliance in the financial system, highlighting the importance of identifying and reporting suspicious activity by financial institutions around the world. With respect to the illicit finance risks posed by MEXC Global, that is of particular importance, as this order addresses primary money laundering concerns that are still ongoing after multiple jurisdictions' financial regulators have issued notices highlighting that MEXC Global has operated in their jurisdictions without the proper license, and in at least one case added the CVC exchanger to a list of suspicious CVC trading platforms.[48]
B. Whether the Prohibition of Certain Transmittals of Funds Would Impose Undue Burdens on Legitimate Activity of MEXC Global or Third Parties
FinCEN has considered whether prohibiting certain transmittals of funds would create a significant competitive disadvantage, including any undue cost or burden associated with compliance, for financial institutions organized or licensed in the United States, as well as the extent to which the action could have a significant adverse systemic impact on legitimate business activities currently being conducted on the MEXC Global platform.[49] Indeed, while MEXC Global is used by licit actors, the legitimate business services that it offers are commonly offered by other regulated institutions, meaning that such licit actors could readily find alternatives to facilitate business.
And, FinCEN assesses that prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global will not present a significant competitive disadvantage for or put an undue burden on financial institutions organized or licensed in the United States. Compliance with the prohibition on certain transmittals of funds set out in this order requires no tools or competencies other than those already employed by domestic financial institutions to maintain their current AML/CFT compliance programs. To aid covered U.S. financial institutions with compliance, FinCEN has elected to provide within this order for the rejection of certain transmittals of CVC that are received from or originate at MEXC Global and outline the steps a covered financial institution should take in such circumstances. In providing for the rejection of CVC under certain limited circumstances, FinCEN acknowledges that, at this time, there are technological limitations that may limit or preclude covered financial institutions from declining CVC transfers originating at addresses outside of their control, and compliant institutions may find themselves in receipt of CVC from MEXC Global despite a desire and effort to limit such exposure.[50] This order therefore allows covered financial institutions the flexibility to act with discretion based on the facts and circumstances of a particular transaction and comply with this order, even where the originating address is no longer accessible, where, for example, (1) CVC transfers originated from MEXC Global, but were held for an extended period of time in an unhosted wallet, or (2) the covered financial institution's risk mitigation procedures would preclude returning funds to MEXC Global. Moreover, by providing for the rejection of CVC, this order ensures that covered financial institutions will not be subject to an undue cost or burden associated with compliance.
C. Whether Any Other Reasonable Alternatives or Special Measures Would Adequately Address the Money Laundering Concern
Before deciding to impose a prohibition on certain transmittals of funds, FinCEN considered other available special measures.[51] After due ( printed page 72426) consideration, FinCEN has determined that a special measure prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global is the appropriate means to adequately address the illicit finance risks posed by MEXC Global.
None of the special measures set out in 31 U.S.C. 5318A—special measures one through five—would effectively address the illicit finance threat posed by MEXC Global. Any additional recordkeeping, information collection, or reporting requirements, as described in 31 U.S.C. 5318A(b)(1)-(4), would be insufficient to guard against the risks posed by covered financial institutions processing transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global. Those special measures would allow such transfers to continue to the benefit of illicit actors connected to Russian illicit finance, as well as Iran-related and other illicit financial activity. Further, merely prohibiting and/or placing conditions upon the opening or maintaining in the United States of correspondent accounts or payable-through accounts for or on behalf of MEXC Global, as described in 31 U.S.C. 5318A(b)(5), would be similarly inadequate. Neither prohibiting nor imposing conditions on such accounts would safeguard the U.S. financial system to the same degree as prohibiting transmittals of funds, as such a special measure would not address the movement of funds outside of a strict correspondent or payable-through relationship, for example, through the movement of funds outside the traditional banking relationship, which may permit MEXC Global to access USD through indirect correspondent relationships via other foreign financial institutions.
D. Whether the Prohibition Should Be Imposed by Order or Regulation
Pursuant to section 9714, the Secretary may impose one or more special measures, including a prohibition on certain transmittals of funds, “by order, regulation or otherwise as permitted by law.” In determining the appropriate approach in this instance, FinCEN considered imposing the prohibition by order or regulation, taking into account the nature of the underlying threat, and determined that proceeding by an order is the most appropriate course of action given the imminent threats posed by the illicit actors whose transactions and access to funds MEXC Global facilitates, as well as the ongoing transactions associated with suspected activity related to Russian illicit finance that continue to be processed through MEXC Global. Further, FinCEN has assessed that this order will not be unduly burdensome or impose new or unique compliance costs on financial institutions.

Section 5 of Executive Order 14294 directs that all future notices of proposed rulemaking (NPRMs) and final rules published in the Federal Register , the violation of which may constitute criminal regulatory offenses, should include a statement identifying that the rule or proposed rule is a criminal regulatory offense and the authorizing statute.[52] Executive Order 14294 directs agencies to draft this statement in consultation with the Department of Justice.
Executive Order 14294 further directs that the regulatory text of all NPRMs and final rules with criminal consequences published in the Federal Register after May 9, 2025, should explicitly state a mens rea requirement for each element of a criminal regulatory offense, accompanied by citations to the relevant provisions of the authorizing statute.
Willful violations of any final regulations set forth in this order may be subject to criminal penalties pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 5322 and regulations promulgated in 31 CFR Chapter X. The statutory authority for criminal liability requires a mens rea of willfulness as an element pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 5322(a) and 31 U.S.C. 5322(b). FinCEN's existing regulation, 31 CFR 1010.840, that sets out criminal penalties for violations of regulations promulgated in 31 CFR Chapter X also includes a mens rea of willfulness. In drafting this statement, FinCEN has consulted with the Department of Justice.
The order defines “MEXC Global,” a Seychelles-based CVC exchanger, to include its branches, subsidiaries, and offices operating as a financial institution in any jurisdiction outside of the United States, and any successor entities. For the purposes of this order, a successor entity means any person that replaces MEXC Global, its branches, subsidiaries, and offices by acquiring its assets, in whole or in part, and/or carrying on the affairs of MEXC Global under a new name. This includes, but is not limited to, any entities referenced in this order as being branches, subsidiaries, or offices of MEXC Global operating as a financial institution in any jurisdiction outside of the United States. Any branches, subsidiaries, and offices of MEXC Global located in the United States are expressly excluded from the definition of “MEXC Global” for the purposes of this order.
2. Convertible Virtual Currency
The order defines “convertible virtual currency” (CVC) as a medium of exchange that either has an equivalent value to currency, or acts as a substitute for currency, but lacks legal tender status. Bitcoin, despite having legal tender status in at least one jurisdiction, is included as a type of CVC for the purpose of this order.
3. Covered Financial Institution
The order defines “covered financial institution” as having the same meaning as “financial institution” in 31 CFR 1010.100(t).
The order defines “transmittals of funds” as the sending and receiving of funds, including CVC. For avoidance of doubt, for this section, this definition of transmittal of funds applies rather than the definition of “transmittal of funds” in section 1010.100(ddd).
5. Meaning of Other Terms
All terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning set forth in 31 CFR chapter X and 31 U.S.C. 5312.
B. Prohibition on Transmittals of Funds Involving MEXC Global
A covered financial institution is prohibited from engaging in any transmittal of funds from or to MEXC Global.
The terms of this order are effective December 10, 2026, with no cessation date.
D. Reservation of Authority
FinCEN reserves authority to impose conditions on certain transmittals of funds from or to MEXC Global and to grant appropriate exemptions from the requirements of this order. ( printed page 72427)
Nothing in this order shall be construed to modify, impair, or otherwise affect any requirements or obligations to which a covered financial institution is subject pursuant to the BSA, including, but not limited to, the filing of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs), or other applicable laws or regulations, such as the sanctions administered and enforced by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control.
F. Penalties for Noncompliance
The covered financial institution, and any of its officers, directors, employees, and agents, may be liable for civil or criminal penalties under 31 U.S.C. 5321 and 5322 for willfully violating this order.
Any judicial determination that any provision of this order is invalid shall not affect the validity of any other provision of this order, and each other provision shall thereafter remain in full force and effect.

Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Department of Transportation (DOT).
The final rule updates the maintenance inspection requirements for single-engine turbine-powered airplanes and unmanned aircraft. Aircraft owners and operators now have more inspection program options to choose from and more relaxed mechanical reliability reporting requirements. It also clarifies various maintenance-related regulations. This final rule relieves aircraft owners, operators, maintenance providers, and FAA of certain workload burdens by facilitating a more efficient workload for these individuals without compromising aviation safety.
Effective January 11, 2027.
